status: Initial editorial annotations, not official ratings or a playtesting certificate.
scale: 0–3 strength of a design signal. Missing fields remain unannotated.

purposes.washerwoman: Starting Townsfolk identity clue that can build a social trust pair.
purposes.librarian: Starting Outsider identity or absence clue; helps examine the Outsider count.
purposes.investigator: Starting Minion identity clue and early evil suspicion.
purposes.chef: Starting count of adjacent evil pairs; supports positional deduction.
purposes.empath: Recurring alignment count for living neighbours; deaths change the information frontier.
purposes.fortuneteller: Player-directed recurring Demon detection, with a personal red herring.
purposes.undertaker: Learns the character of yesterday's executed player; makes execution an information investment.
purposes.monk: Protects another player from the Demon for one night.
purposes.ravenkeeper: Rewards dying at night with a chosen character-information check.
purposes.virgin: First nomination can immediately execute a Townsfolk nominator, creating conditional confirmation.
purposes.slayer: One public attempt to kill a Demon; success can decisively resolve a suspect.
purposes.soldier: Passive safety from the Demon; creates explanations for failed night kills.
purposes.mayor: Alternative good victory at three alive with no execution; possible death redirection complicates attacks.
purposes.butler: Voting restriction tied to a chosen master; changes public voting discipline.
purposes.drunk: A hidden Outsider who believes they have a Townsfolk ability, introducing an unreliable claim.
purposes.recluse: Optional evil and evil-character registration; destabilises character and alignment tests.
purposes.saint: Execution creates an immediate good loss, making the claim a high-stakes social decision.
purposes.poisoner: Targeted night-and-day ability disruption creates competing information worlds.
purposes.spy: Grimoire knowledge supports evil planning; optional good registration supports false confirmation.
purposes.scarletwoman: Conditional backup Demon when the current Demon dies with enough players alive.
purposes.baron: Adds Outsiders at setup, reshaping the good team's ability mix and plausible Outsider claims.
purposes.imp: Night kills with optional self-kill succession into an alive Minion.
purposes.chambermaid: Checks whether two chosen alive players woke tonight due to their abilities.
purposes.exorcist: A correct Demon choice prevents its wake that night and gives the Demon information about the Exorcist.
purposes.gambler: Chosen character guesses risk the Gambler's life; survival supports but does not universally confirm a claim.
purposes.gossip: Public statements can produce night deaths when true; death attribution is central.
purposes.grandmother: Starts knowing a good player and their character; a Demon kill of that player can cause a linked death.
purposes.courtier: Once-per-game choice of a character disables that character through drunkenness for three nights and days.
purposes.innkeeper: Protects two players from death tonight while making one drunk until dusk.
purposes.minstrel: A Minion execution makes almost everyone else drunk, changing both information and death patterns.
purposes.pacifist: Good executed players might survive; a survival is not universal hard confirmation.
purposes.professor: One resurrection of a dead Townsfolk, producing a strong visible event when it succeeds.
purposes.fool: Survives the first death event; survival complicates the interpretation of executions and attacks.
purposes.sailor: Chooses an alive player; one becomes drunk, and the sober Sailor cannot die.
purposes.tealady: Protects both alive neighbours from death when both are good; makes position and survival informative.
purposes.tinker: May die at any time, adding discretionary death uncertainty.
purposes.moonchild: When learning they died, publicly chooses an alive player; a good choice dies tonight.
purposes.goon: The first ability chooser targeting the Goon becomes drunk, and the Goon changes alignment to theirs.
purposes.lunatic: Believes they are a Demon, while the real Demon receives information about their identity and choices.
purposes.devilsadvocate: Chosen alive players survive execution tomorrow, providing evil explanations for survival.
purposes.assassin: One extra kill that bypasses ordinary inability-to-die protections.
purposes.godfather: Learns in-play Outsiders and gains kills following Outsider deaths; changes the setup count.
purposes.mastermind: Continues the game after a Demon execution and makes the next day's execution alignment decisive.
purposes.zombuul: Conditional kills and a first apparent death while still alive; makes apparent death unreliable.
purposes.pukka: Poisons a chosen player, then kills its previous target and restores that target's health.
purposes.shabaloth: Two night-kill choices with possible resurrection of a previously chosen dead player.
purposes.po: Can skip a kill to enable a three-player attack on the next night.
purposes.clockmaker: Starting distance between the Demon and nearest Minion; provides positional evil information.
purposes.dreamer: Returns a good and an evil character option for a chosen player, including the correct character.
purposes.mathematician: Tracks abnormal ability operation due to another character's ability, rather than directly identifying the affected player.
purposes.flowergirl: Learns whether a Demon voted today; encourages controlled public vote experiments.
purposes.towncrier: Learns whether a Minion nominated today; connects nominations to evil possibilities.
purposes.oracle: Counts dead evil players each night after the first; makes deaths an alignment-information resource.
purposes.savant: Receives two private statements each day, one true and one false.
purposes.seamstress: One alignment comparison between two other players.
purposes.juggler: Public first-day character guesses produce a count of correct guesses tonight.
purposes.artist: One private yes/no question to the Storyteller.
purposes.philosopher: Gains a good character's ability; makes an existing holder of that character drunk.
purposes.snakecharmer: Alignment checks that swap character and alignment with a chosen Demon and poison the former Demon.
purposes.sage: If killed by the Demon, learns a two-player Demon candidate pair.
purposes.mutant: Risk of execution if mad about being an Outsider; puts pressure on truthful public identity.
purposes.sweetheart: Death makes a player drunk, creating an ongoing information-reliability problem.
purposes.barber: Death enables the Demon to offer a character swap between two non-Demons.
purposes.klutz: Learning of death triggers a public alive-player choice; choosing evil loses immediately.
purposes.eviltwin: Two players know opposing-alignment counterparts; executing the good twin loses and blocks normal good victory while both live.
purposes.witch: Curses a chosen player's next-day nomination to cause death, unless the live-player threshold removes the ability.
purposes.cerenovus: Forces a player to be mad about a selected good character or risk execution.
purposes.pithag: Changes a player's character to a not-in-play character; creating a Demon makes tonight's deaths arbitrary.
purposes.fanggu: The first Outsider kill transfers Demonhood to that Outsider; adds an Outsider at setup.
purposes.vigormortis: Killed Minions retain their abilities and poison a Townsfolk neighbour; removes an Outsider at setup.
purposes.nodashii: Night kills plus continuous poisoning of the two nearest Townsfolk neighbours.
purposes.vortox: Forces false Townsfolk information and requires an execution each day to avoid an evil victory.
purposes.acrobat: Tests a chosen player's drunk or poisoned state through a conditional self-death.
purposes.alchemist: A Townsfolk with a Minion ability; requires careful ability selection and relevant jinx handling.
purposes.alsaahir: Public complete Minion/Demon guesses can create an immediate good win.
purposes.amnesiac: Unknown Storyteller-specified ability with daily accuracy feedback; this app must not invent that ability.
purposes.atheist: A no-evil setup and Storyteller-rule-breaking win condition requiring a specially designed script.
purposes.balloonist: Recurring character-type changes in player information, with optional added Outsider.
purposes.banshee: A Demon kill is publicly announced and grants extra nominations and votes after death.
purposes.bountyhunter: Tracks an evil player and refreshes after their death; creates an evil Townsfolk at setup.
purposes.cannibal: Uses the last execution victim's ability, but an evil victim causes poisoning until a good execution death.
purposes.choirboy: After a Demon kill of the King, learns the Demon; depends on King being on the script.
purposes.cultleader: Changes alignment based on an alive neighbour; a cult agreement can produce an immediate win for its alignment.
purposes.engineer: One opportunity to choose which Minions or Demon are in play, changing the mechanical world.
purposes.farmer: A night death turns an alive good player into a Farmer, enabling chains of claims.
purposes.fisherman: One private request for Storyteller advice that helps the good team win.
purposes.general: Recurring subjective report of which alignment is winning.
purposes.highpriestess: Recurring Storyteller pointer to a player to talk to; requires contextual guidance.
purposes.huntsman: One choice to convert the Damsel to a Townsfolk; requires Damsel in setup.
purposes.king: Learns an alive character when the dead equal or outnumber the living; the Demon knows the King.
purposes.knight: Starts knowing two non-Demons, creating a bounded Demon-elimination clue.
purposes.lycanthrope: A successful chosen good-player kill can replace ordinary night deaths, altering death attribution.
purposes.magician: Distorts evil-team starting information, causing uncertainty about allies.
purposes.nightwatchman: One other player learns who the Nightwatchman is; creates a private confirmation link.
purposes.noble: Starts knowing three players of whom exactly one is evil.
purposes.pixie: Starts knowing an in-play Townsfolk and may gain its ability after their death if sufficiently mad about being it.
purposes.poppygrower: Prevents evil players learning who each other are until the Poppy Grower dies.
purposes.preacher: Chosen Minions learn this and lose their abilities, reducing evil utility.
purposes.princess: A first-day nomination and execution can prevent the Demon's kill tonight.
purposes.shugenja: Starts knowing the direction of the closest evil player.
purposes.villageidiot: Recurring chosen alignment information, with optional extra copies and a drunk extra.
purposes.damsel: A publicly correct Minion guess of the Damsel loses for good; hidden identity creates social pressure.
purposes.golem: One nomination that kills the nominee unless they are the Demon.
purposes.hatter: Death permits Minion and Demon character changes, potentially invalidating earlier worlds.
purposes.heretic: Reverses which team wins, even if dead, fundamentally changing victory interpretation.
purposes.hermit: Combines every Outsider ability on the script, introducing many dependencies and possible failure conditions.
purposes.ogre: Starts choosing a friend and joins their alignment without learning it.
purposes.plaguedoctor: Death gives the Storyteller a Minion ability; demands specific interaction and jinx review.
purposes.politician: Can win with evil if most responsible for good losing; creates a personal incentive to undermine good.
purposes.puzzlemaster: Makes one player drunk; one correct identification of that player reveals the Demon, otherwise produces false Demon information.
purposes.snitch: Gives Minions three not-in-play characters, broadening coordinated evil bluffs.
purposes.zealot: Must vote for every nomination while enough players are alive.
purposes.boffin: Gives the Demon a not-in-play good ability; demands detailed ability and jinx review.
purposes.boomdandy: Execution kills most players and triggers a timed final decision.
purposes.fearmonger: Chooses a player; a qualifying nomination, execution and death ends the game in the opposite alignment's favour.
purposes.goblin: Claiming Goblin when nominated creates an evil execution-win threat.
purposes.harpy: Madness pressure about an evil accusation can cause deaths if not followed.
purposes.marionette: An evil Minion believes they are good; the Demon knows their identity and they neighbour the Demon.
purposes.mezepheles: Knowing and eliciting a secret word turns the first good speaker evil that night.
purposes.organgrinder: Blind voting and special self-execution vote conditions change public social evidence.
purposes.psychopath: Daytime public kills and a roshambo condition for death by execution.
purposes.summoner: Creates an evil Demon on the third night; starts with no Demon and requires compatible setup and jinx handling.
purposes.vizier: Public Minion identity, daytime immortality, and conditional immediate execution control.
purposes.widow: Starts with Grimoire knowledge and persistent chosen poisoning; a good player learns a Widow is in play.
purposes.wizard: One wish whose effects are adjudicated by the Storyteller; this app does not invent wishes or their effects.
purposes.wraith: Wakes with evil players and may open their eyes at night, exposing evil coordination.
purposes.xaan: Poisons all Townsfolk on a setup-defined night X; Outsider count defines timing.
purposes.alhadikhia: Three publicly named players privately choose life or death; all choosing life causes all three deaths.
purposes.kazali: Chooses Minions at setup and can change the Outsider count freely; requires nonstandard setup review.
purposes.legion: A majority-evil Legion setup with group kill and voting rules that change the normal game structure.
purposes.leviathan: A five-day game with execution-dependent evil wins rather than ordinary night kills.
purposes.lilmonsta: Minions choose a babysitter who counts as the Demon; extra Minion and Storyteller-chosen deaths.
purposes.lleech: Continuous poisoned host determines the Demon's death; the Demon survives while the host lives.
purposes.lordoftyphon: Night kills with a fixed evil line, extra Minion and flexible Outsider count.
purposes.ojo: Chooses a character to kill; absent characters transfer kill control to the Storyteller.
purposes.riot: Day-three nomination deaths and replacement of evil characters make a distinct endgame.
purposes.yaggababble: Public repetition of a secret phrase can produce Storyteller-controlled deaths.

amnesiac: The app does not create an Amnesiac ability. Import/retheme is supported; bespoke ability design stays with the Storyteller.
atheist: Requires a specially designed no-evil setup; conventional evil-team analysis is not applicable.
wizard: The app does not invent a wish or its consequences. Storyteller adjudication is required.
heretic: Win inversion changes incentives for every team; standard evil/good strategy assumptions need a full review.
hermit: Every Outsider ability on the script matters; inspect the complete Outsider list and relevant jinxes.
summoner: Starts with no Demon in play. The listed Demons are candidates for creation, not ordinary starting Demon choices.
legion: Majority-evil setup and special voting rules invalidate ordinary team-count assumptions.
riot: Changes the day-three endgame and evil setup. Review nomination chains and applicable jinxes.
lilmonsta: No ordinary player holds the Demon character. Review babysitting, extra Minion setup and Storyteller kills.
kazali: Selected Minions and arbitrary Outsider count change normal setup assumptions.
lordoftyphon: Extra Minion, variable Outsiders and positional evil setup require separate setup review.
boffin: List plausible not-in-play good abilities and consult all relevant jinxes before running.
alchemist: List the possible Minion abilities and consult all relevant jinxes before running.
villageidiot: Extra Village Idiots may be in play with one extra drunk. Script record count is not an in-play multiplicity simulator.
